extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political economy / classical economics
extracted.subtask_description: Explanation of classical political-economy principles governing market price, natural price, and the determination of wages, rent, and profit; includes causes of price fluctuations and social/institutional effects. Suitable as an extract for study of 18th-century economic theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural price as the central price
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural price is 'the central price, to which the prices of all commodities are continually gravitating.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market prices fluctuate above or below this centre because of accidents, natural causes, or policy, but they are constantly tending towards the natural price; the natural price is the long-run equilibrium around which temporary deviations occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectual demand determines market price via supply
rubrics_metrics.description: When quantity brought to market falls short of the effectual demand, competition among buyers raises market price above the natural price; when quantity exceeds effectual demand, competition among sellers drives market price below the natural price; when quantity exactly supplies effectual demand, market price approximates the natural price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: blockade or famine (necessaries become exorbitant); importation of perishables (large downward pressure); when supply equals effectual demand the whole quantity can be sold at the natural price and not for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price components: rent, wages, and profit
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole price of a commodity resolves into its components: rent (land), wages (labour), and profit (stock).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occasional and temporary fluctuations chiefly affect the parts resolving into wages and profit; rent (especially certain money rent) is less affected. Leases and rents are typically set against average, not temporary, prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perishability and production variability affect price stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Industries whose output varies year-to-year (e.g., agriculture: corn, wine, oil) cause greater market-price fluctuations than industries with steady annual output (e.g., spinners and weavers producing cloth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because agricultural output can differ widely from its average produce, market price for such commodities varies much more; linen and woollen cloth prices vary mainly with demand, not large supply swings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market self-adjustment through factor mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: If any component of price is paid below its natural rate, owners of that factor withdraw land, labour, or stock from the employment until quantity supplied returns to match the effectual demand; if components rise above natural rate, other owners are prompted to employ more factors until return to natural rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mobility of factors tends to restore all parts of price to their natural rates and the whole price to its natural price in the long run, assuming liberty of movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrets and concealed extraordinary profits can delay entry and sustain above-natural prices
rubrics_metrics.description: When suppliers conceal knowledge of an increased effectual demand or extraordinary profits, they can delay rival entry and enjoy extraordinary profits for some time; secrets in manufactures can be kept longer than trade secrets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dyer who discovers cheaper methods may enjoy repeated extraordinary profits (seen as high wages of private labour) for life and pass them to posterity; however, such secrets are seldom kept indefinitely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monopoly yields highest extractable price by understocking market
rubrics_metrics.description: A monopoly keeps the market understocked relative to effectual demand and thus sells at a price 'much above the natural price.' The monopoly price is 'the highest which can be got.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monopolists' behavior mirrors that of those who keep secrets; monopoly effects can be long-lasting depending on the grant of the monopoly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory restraints (corporations, apprenticeship statutes) raise prices/wages/profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive privileges of corporations, apprenticeships, and laws that restrain competition function as enlarged monopolies and tend to keep market prices, wages, and profits above natural rates, sometimes for very long periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such enhancements of market price endure as long as the policies that create them; they can maintain elevated returns across whole classes of employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market price rarely remains long below natural price under liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: When any part of price is paid below its natural rate, those whose interest is affected immediately feel the loss and withdraw factors, so the quantity brought to market falls and market price rises to natural price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The upward correction happens relatively quickly where there is perfect liberty and ability of factors to withdraw from unprofitable employments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wages as the produce of labour and deductions by rent and profit
rubrics_metrics.description: In a primitive state the produce of labour constituted the whole recompense of labour; once land is appropriated and stock accumulates, rent (to landlords) and profit (to masters) are first deductions from the produce, leaving wages as the portion after those deductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent workmen who own their stock enjoy both wages and profits, but most workers serve under masters who advance maintenance and materials, thus sharing the produce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common wages depend on bargaining between workmen and masters
rubrics_metrics.description: Common wages of labour are determined by the contract between labourers and masters, whose interests differ: workmen wish higher wages, masters want to give less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Masters are fewer and can more easily combine (tacitly or explicitly) to keep wages down; laws often allow masters' combinations and forbid workmen's, making masters' position stronger in disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a subsistence floor for wages (lowest consistent with common humanity)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a certain rate below which ordinary wages cannot be reduced for any considerable time: wages must at least suffice for a labourer's maintenance and usually somewhat more to allow rearing a family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cantillon's argument is cited: lowest labour must earn at least double maintenance to ensure generational replacement; precise proportion not fixed by author, but the principle of a subsistence minimum holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increasing national revenue and stock raises wages via higher demand for labour
rubrics_metrics.description: When revenue and stock (funds to pay wages) increase, demand for wage-labour rises because masters employ more servants or journeymen; thus wages rise in growing societies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wages are higher not in the absolutely richest countries but in the most thriving—those with rapid increases in wealth (example: higher wages in 18th-century North America vs England).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stationary wealth/population leads to lower wages
rubrics_metrics.description: If a country's wealth and stock have been long stationary, wages tend to be low because the supply of labour is sufficient to meet demand and masters need not bid for hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: China described as long stationary with low wages and difficulty for labourers to raise a family; contrast with thriving colonies where wages are higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinations and labour conflicts often fail without sustained resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Workmen's combinations to raise wages are often loud and sometimes violent but usually fail because of magistrate intervention, masters' steadiness, and workers' immediate need for subsistence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While combinations of masters to keep wages down are tacit and enduring, workmen's open combinations tend to be short-lived and risk punishment or ruin of leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic and familial economics influence labour supply and wages
rubrics_metrics.description: High value of children and early marriage in thriving colonies increase population rapidly, affecting the supply of labour; in thriving societies a family can be a source of wealth which influences wages and labour availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: North American colonies saw rapid population doubling and higher real wages and lower prices of provisions, making child labour economically valuable and encouraging early marriage.
